## The Definition of Done (the gate)
A ticket is **APPROVED-READY only if EVERY item below holds**. If even ONE is unmet, the ticket
is **BLOCKED** and the PM comment must name the exact missing item(s). (All-or-nothing.)

1. **Acceptance met** — every acceptance / "Definition of Done" line in the ticket description AND
   every concrete ask in the latest product owner comment is satisfied.
2. **Merged to dev** — the change is present on `origin/dev` of the owning repo (not just on a
   feature branch). A pushed branch with no merge = NOT done.
3. **Deployed** — the service is live on dev: ArgoCD `<svc>-dev` Application is **Synced + Healthy**
   (image tag bumped in `infra-gitops/envs/dev/services/<svc>/values.yaml` after merge).
4. **Tests green** — the coverage the OWNING REPO can actually run passes. Verified mapping
   (2026-08-20, by inspecting the repos):

   | (various authors) | Framework |
   |---|---|
   | `admin-frontend` (React/TS) | Cypress (`*-sdNNNN.cy.ts`) + Vitest |
   | `chat-service`, `commandcenter-service` (Python) | pytest under `tests/` |
   | `*-api`, `*-consumer` (.NET) | xUnit in the `*.Tests` project |
   | cross-service API / load / contract | k6, which exists ONLY in `testing-k6` |

   **A DoD line naming a framework the repo cannot run is a defect in the TICKET, not in the work.**
   The team copy-pastes "Cypress Tests implemented (frontend) / K6 Tests implemented (backend)" onto
   every ticket; `chat-service` has no k6 module at all, and asserting wording or LLM narration through
   k6 is flaky by construction. At review:
   - coverage **absent entirely** -> still BLOCKS, unchanged;
   - coverage present in the repo's **native** framework while the DoD names another -> NOT the dev's
     failure. Name the tests that do exist, say plainly that the DoD line is mis-specified, and let
     Paul waive that line explicitly. Never waive it silently, and never fail a dev for not writing a
     test their service cannot run.
   Precedent: SD-5679/SD-5709 (Cypress named, label-only change) and SD-5458/SD-5691 (K6 named, Python
   service with targeted pytest) were all waived this way on 2026-08-20.

**Live-verify is N/A until 2 and 3 hold.** For unmerged work, report branch-level findings only and
mark BLOCKED on "not merged to dev" — never claim a live PASS/FAIL for something never deployed.

### A ticket with NO Definition of Done section cannot be approved (Paul, 2026-08-31)
An absent checklist is not an empty one. Judging against a bar we invented lets a ticket pass a test
the reviewer never applies, and that is how work gets approved and then bounced.

- No DoD section in the description means **BLOCKED**, and the missing item is the DoD itself.
- **Authoring it belongs to the product owner, not the assignee and not us.** In the developer
  self-check this is the `FIX: PO` tag: the author cannot close it and must not be asked to.
- Measured: 48 of 60 To Be Checked tickets had no DoD section on 2026-08-28, and 9 of the 28 tickets
  reverted from Approved. This is the majority path, not a corner case.

### The merged-code bar: observed, not agreed
The PO verification run applies "only merged code counts as proof of completion", and it has
**overridden a ticket's own compliant DoD**. Proof: SD-5303 asks for eval results, a Confluence
recommendation and a team review, names no code anywhere, carries a linked fix receipt, and was still
reverted on 2026-08-31 with exactly that sentence.

This is recorded as an observed rule with its date, never as policy, so it can be retired in one edit
if the PO changes it. It is **a warning, never a blocker**: SD-5413 was accepted with no code at all
under a "small-UI policy" that is written down nowhere, so the bar is not applied absolutely.

At review, and in the developer self-check: when the lane 2b feature search returns
`NOT_FOUND_AFTER_5_SEARCHES`, say the ticket will likely be bounced for carrying no commit,
**whatever its DoD demands**. Do not convert that into an unmet DoD item unless the DoD actually asks
for merged code.

### Where the work lives when no branch carries the ticket key
Several of the team put multiple tickets on ONE branch, so a missing `SD-XXXX` branch is normal and
is never a finding on its own. When the work is confirmed but rides another branch, the review comment
must name all five facts: carrying branch, sibling ticket key, PR number and state, merge commit on
`origin/dev`, and merge date. The PO checks this work himself and only he sets Done; without the
locator he searches for a branch that was never created. "It is on another branch" is the same dead
end with more words.

## What a receipt is

A short Confluence page written **after a non-trivial fix lands**, capturing what broke, what fixed
it, and what is left to watch, so the next engineer hitting a similar issue finds the prior work
instead of re-investigating.

It is **not** a post-mortem. No timelines, no five-whys, no action items needing approval. One page
per fix, written by the person who landed the fix, under an hour, 300 to 800 words. Code snippets
and tables do not count toward the budget.


## Canonical pages (Confluence, site `simedia-data.atlassian.net`)

| (various authors) | id | (various authors) |
|---|---|---|
| Fix Receipts — Process (SD-4540) | `568066050` | The rules. Also the **parent** every receipt goes under |
| Fix Receipt — Template | `568098817` | Copy-this-page template, ten sections |
| Fix Receipts — Adoption & Rollout (SD-4623) | `579731469` | The Done gate and the rollout log |

Read a page: `GET /wiki/rest/api/content/<id>?expand=body.view,version`
Owner of all three: Paul. Space: `Data!`, path `Data! > Documentations > Processes & Conventions`.


## The five triggers (any ONE makes a receipt owed)

1. Touched a shared library, auth flow, infrastructure or cluster config, or anything used by 3 or
   more services.
2. Root cause is non-obvious from reading the diff (the bug looked like one thing, was another).
3. The investigation produced evidence useful beyond the immediate fix (logs, run output, cluster
   state).
4. The same failure has been hit before. The receipt exists to break the loop.
5. A reviewer or PM explicitly asked for one.

**Knowable at ticket-creation time:** 1, 4, 5. Those may carry a receipt DoD line from the start.
**Only knowable after the fix exists:** 2 and 3. Those surface at review as an advisory flag, never
as a retroactive DoD item.


## The skip list is RETIRED (Paul, 2026-08-26)

**There is no skip list any more. Every ticket needs a receipt, with no exemption for size.**

Paul was shown the board impact before deciding and reaffirmed: 71 of 103 in To Be Checked and 62 of
80 Approved fail this bar. He took it anyway. Do not re-litigate it per run, and do not quietly grant
an exemption because a change looks trivial.

What changed my own argument against it: the skip list was defended on the grounds that demanding a
page for a one-line tooltip reword is unreasonable. Measured on 2026-08-26, a developer had written a
receipt for every one of those anyway. The team was never resisting the receipt, only the link. So
the exemption was protecting against a cost nobody was actually paying.

PRIOR TEXT, retained so the reversal is legible to anyone who learned the old rule:

> Trivial typo fixes, dependency bumps with no behaviour change, UI copy edits, and any fix small
> enough that the PR description already says everything worth saying.
> This list is load-bearing. Demanding a receipt on a copy edit makes the DoD unsatisfiable on
> trivial work, and a DoD item that gets ticked without being done devalues the other items.


## Where a receipt lives, and how it links back

- **Title:** `<TICKET-ID> — <one-line summary>`, e.g. `SD-4464 — K6 Authentication Resilience`
- **Parent:** page `568066050`
- **In the page:** paste the full `https://simedia-data.atlassian.net/browse/SD-XXXX` URL at the top
  so Confluence renders a smart-link card
- **On the ticket:** one comment on close, format `Receipt: <confluence URL>`

A page that exists but is not linked on the ticket does **not** satisfy a DoD item. Same rule as the
DOC lane.


## Searching for one (two conventions exist, search BOTH)

The convention has split in practice. A search on one form alone produces a false negative.

| (various authors) | Where it lives | Who writes it |
|---|---|---|
| `<KEY> — <summary>` | under page `568066050` | (various authors) |
| `Fix Receipt: <KEY> - <summary>` | under `Backend Services & APIs` or `Frontend & Dashboard UI` | a developer (4), the product owner (1) |

```
GET /wiki/rest/api/search?cql=title ~ "<KEY>"        # catches both forms
GET /wiki/rest/api/content/568066050/child/page      # what is actually filed under the process page
```

Do not report "no receipt" off a single-form search. Run the title search, and only then claim
absence, quoting the command per the absence-claim rule in `simedia-pm.md`.


## Required sections (from template `568098817`)

Status · Ticket / First detected / Repo touched · Root cause · Fix · Regression checks done · Files
changed · Coverage trade-offs · Out of scope, flagged elsewhere · DoD mapping · How to verify after
deploy.

Skip a section that genuinely does not apply by annotating it `n/a — <reason>`. Never delete the
heading.
